content:
maria: FYI customer acme-123 reporting streaming gen ends with `broken pipe` ~45s in, then they get billed as a 5xx. ticket #12345, attaching customer trace.

jordan: Link to trace? can you paste the request-id? I want to check gateway logs.

maria: request-id=tr-0a1b2c3d. trace attached in ticket.

jordan: I pulled the trace. Gateway logs show `FIN` from the proxy at ~45s before we sent final chunk trailer. Upstream returned chunks then proxy closed connection.

emily: I can repro this pattern locally using an nginx proxy with `proxy_send_timeout` set to 40s. When proxy does FIN before trailer we end up in our EOF heuristic that marks it as server error.

samir: Quick explain: our current accounting treats an EOF without a proper chunked trailer as an unexpected early EOF -> class as 5xx for billing. Problem: if the *client or intermediary* half-closes mid-response, that should be treated as client abort, not server 5xx.

emily: Repro curl example I used:
```bash
curl -v --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-optim","prompt":"stream test\n"}'
```

Proxy config used (nginx):
```nginx
proxy_send_timeout 40s;
proxy_buffering off;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```

jordan: Interesting: the proxy sends `FIN` right after the last data frame, before the chunked trailer. Our gateway sees EOF and no `0\r\n\r\n` trailer -> flags 5xx. We need a better muscle to detect origin of FIN.

samir: Plan: add a small classifier that looks at socket-level close origin and timing. If FIN aligns with client/proxy IP and occurs within 250ms of last chunk, mark as client-initiated close -> don't bill as 5xx. Also emit `streaming.eof.origin` tag for later audits.

maria: Can we hotfix this quickly? Customer is asking for charge review if they were billed incorrectly.

samir: I'll roll a canary with classifier + extra logging. Steps:
- add `streaming.eof.origin` (client|gateway|server)
- if origin==client, mark request as aborted rather than 5xx
- notify billing team with a sample list
ETA ~3h for canary.

emily: I've attached a repro script to the ticket and a short note on how to trigger with nginx. Also included tcpdump snippet showing `FIN` from proxy.

jordan: For telemetry, add a counter `streaming.eof.classified.client_abort` so we can measure how many incidents flip after patch.

maria: Great. Please cc billing once we have samples. Customer wants a timeline for credit if misbilled.

ops-bot: Incident created: INV-789, priority=P2, owner=@samir. Canary pipeline triggered for `stream-eof-classifier` (canary group: streaming-canary-1).

samir: Pushed backend change to canary. Adding logs for request-id=tr-0a1b2c3d. Will monitor for 30m and collect samples for billing.

emily: Confirmed canary saw similar request and it is now classified as `client_abort` in logs. Sample: `streaming.eof.origin=client` for tr-0a1b2c3d.

maria: :thumbsup: Good work. After 1h if metrics look stable we can roll to prod and instruct billing to review the ACME charges.

samir: Will follow up with a PR link and postmortem note once fully rolled out.

ops-bot: Deployment note: `stream-eof-classifier` canary -> started (2024-10-12T14:32:00Z).
